text:
dave: Heads-up: product wants to change webhook delivery payload to include a top-level envelope (meta + events). breaking for customers parsing the old flat payload. need compatibility shims and a rollout plan.

tanya: Oof. We should avoid any breaking change by default. Proposal: opt-in via header X-Redwood-Webhooks: envelope=1 or a tenant flag. Default keep legacy flat payload.

omar: Agree. Also add a probe endpoint for webhook receivers? hard since webhooks are push. Instead we can let receivers POST a verification call to /v1/webhook-capabilities to declare they support envelope. cache per-callback-url.

rachel: Good idea. That call should be authenticated by a token we provide in webhook settings. simple: POST /v1/webhook-capabilities {callback_url, token} -> {supports_envelope:true/false}. store for 48h.

dave: Shim rules: when delivering, if receiver opted-in (header or capability true) -> send envelope. else -> send legacy flat payload. Also allow tenant override: force_envelope=true for testing.

tanya: Telemetry: emit webhook.envelope.sent, webhook.envelope.fallback with tags {tenant, callback_url, event_type}. sample 100% for envelope, 1% fallback. add migration.wave tag for rollout waves.

omar: Delivery semantics: ensure signature header (X-Redwood-Signature) covers canonicalized body. for envelope we must keep signature backwards compatible or version it. prefer versioned signature header: X-Redwood-Signature-V1 for legacy, V2 for envelope. include both when possible to avoid receiver confusion.

rachel: Hmm dual signature may confuse libs. Alternative: compute signature over canonical payload and include X-Redwood-Signature plus X-Redwood-Payload-Version. receivers can verify based on version. keeps single sig header.

dave: I like version tag. implement X-Redwood-Payload-Version: v1|v2 and X-Redwood-Signature (HMAC over bytes). document canonicalization rules.

tanya: Ops flags: webhook.payload.envelope = off|opt-in|force. default opt-in. When force, runtime will send envelope to all callbacks regardless of probe.

omar: Performance: envelope adds a small wrapper, watch payload.size and retries. add metrics: webhook.payload.size.bytes and webhook.send.ms per-version. add alert if p95 send latency increases >20% for any tenant.

rachel: Rollout steps: 1) add webhook-capabilities endpoint + signature/version headers behind off; 2) implement sender shim in staging; 3) invite customer partners to opt-in beta; 4) enable opt-in for internal tenants 10% canary; 5) 25/50/100% ramp; 6) after 8 weeks of stability, offer forced migration and announce deprecation of legacy shape with 6mo lead.

dave: Rollback triggers: delivery error rate spike >2x OR verification failures (signature mismatches) >0.5% OR p95 delivery latency +25% -> automatically fallback that callback_url to legacy and page.

tanya: SDKs & vendor outreach: publish webhook helper that auto-posts capabilities and can toggle header. reach out to major webhook consumer libs with PRs.

omar: Testing: add integration tests that register a fake callback, try v1 and v2 payloads, verify signature checks, and run retry logic. add fuzz tests that mutate rw_meta fields to ensure receivers ignoring unknown fields still pass.

rachel: Security: ensure rw_meta doesn't include secrets or PII. signature algorithm unchanged (HMAC-SHA256), rotate keys procedure documented.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/webhook-envelope -> staging (build 7129). CI: 88/90 tests green.

ops-bot: dashboards added: "webhook.envelope.fallback_rate", "webhook.send_latency_by_version" and alert "webhook.rollback_trigger".

dave: Keep shim focused on shape translation only. No behavioral changes or enrichment. owners: dave (spec + rollout), tanya (runtime + flags), omar (security + signatures). follow up Fri 3pm to review staging metrics.

rachel: ack, i'll write the docs and example for callback operators.

dave: thanks all.
